texts.preamble: Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 In The Court Of Sh. Yashwant Kumar District & Sessions Judge/Fsat, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No. 04/19 (Cnr No. Dlnd010019462019) Sh. Sunil Kumar S/o Sh. Roop Sagar R/o 84/225, Karwalo Nagar Anwerganj, Kanpur (Up) ..... Appellant Versus The State (Food Safety Officer) Department of Food Safety 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Place New Delhi110001 . ..... Respondent Appeal Against The Order Dated 10.12.2018 Of Ld. Adjudicating Officer / Additional District Magistrate, Jam Nagar House, New Delhi. Date of filing of appeal : 29.01.2019 Date of arguments : 09.12.2019 Date of judgment : 11.12.2019 J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that on 24.10.2016, a sample of "Pan Masala" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the premises of Food Business Operator ("FBO" in short) Sh. Prem Chand Jain S/o Late Sh. Nemi Chand Jain, M/s Jain Book Corner and Jain Tobacconist, 42, Bengali Market, New Delhi. The sample was divided into four equal parts and one Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97113668/ 1 counterpart was sent to Food Analyst, Delhi. On analysis by the Food Analyst, Delhi, the said sample was declared to be misbranded vide report dt.28.10.2016 as the complete address of the manufacturer was not declared as required under Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (FPS & FA) Regulations. Consequently, a complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 2 of 11 the Adjudicating Officer. In the present case, the manufacturer has mentioned the address of registered office on the sample commodity as 52/34, Naya Ganj, Kanpur208001 and by writing registered office, address is the complete address. FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 3 of 11 4. The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal.
texts.arguments: 3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter alia on the grounds among others that Ld. ADM has failed to appreciate that the company manufacturer of the sampled commodity has not been arrayed as accused/one of the respondents. The appellant has neither supplied the sampled commodity nor has any business dealings with respondent no. 1 to 3 and that Sh. Prem Chand Jain, the Business Operator has clearly mentioned in his reply that the sample commodity was purchased from the market through selling agent Sh. Krishan Kumar, but he has never visited premises of the company and Sh. Prem Chand Jain replied to the FSO during investigation that the sample commodity was purchased from the market and no bill was issued on demand. Therefore, the appellant has no concern with the sample commodity and unnecessarily has been penalized by the Ld. ADM. Nobody can be prosecuted merely on the label declaration in the absence of purchased bill, invoice, purchased memorandum etc. 6. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that as per the Food Analyst report dated 28.10.2016, there is no food adulteration. There is an allegation by the respondent that complete address was not mentioned on the label of the sampled commodity. Whereas, the appellant herein was the nominee of the manufacturer company and penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ was imposed upon him. The appellant is not aware who is Krishan Kumar and why the appellant has been impleaded in this case. Ld. Counsel for the appellant, in support of his arguments, has relied upon the judgments in the cases of M/s Parakh Foods Ltd. versus State of A.P. & Anr. 2008 (1) FAC 150; Bhola Ram versus The State of Punjab in Criminal Revision No. 1144 of 1984 decided by Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court on 31.01.1985; Mohinder Kumar versus State of Haryana 2004 (1) FAC 65 SCI; M/s Murlidhar Shyamlal and another versus State of Assam in Criminal Appeal No. 127 of 1996 decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India on 18.01.1996; Aneeta Hada versus Godfather Travels and Tours (P) Limited (2012) 5 Supreme Court Cases 661; Sham Sunder Bassi versus The State of Punjab in Criminal Misc. No. 6744 M of 1987 decided by Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court on 08.05.1991; Hindustan Lever versus Govt Food Inspector 2011 (2) FAC 407; Epic Food Products Pvt. Ltd. and other versus State of Haryana and another in Criminal Misc. No. M1545 of 2010 decided by Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court on 18.07.2011; R.K. Mittal versus Dr. B. Roy Chaudhury and another in Criminal Revision No. 118 of 1981 decided by Hon'ble Calcutta High Court on 03.05.1984; Rallis India Ltd. versus Podhuru Vidya Bhusan & others 2012 (2) FAC 360; State of Orissa versus Rabindra Sahu 2006 FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 5 of 11 (1) FAC 200 and in the case of Rameshwar Dayal versus State of U.P. in Criminal Appeal No. 231 of 1981 decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India on 30.04.1992. 7. Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent has argued that the present case pertains to label declaration. The Ld. Chief PP for the State, in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar versus The State of Uttar Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No. 1541 of 2019 decided on 04.10.2019 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. 8. In the present case, the appellant has challenged the impugned order dt.10.12.2018 mainly on the grounds that the appellant cannot be penalised for the offence of misbranding in the absence of purchased bill, invoice, purchased memorandum etc. The Food Analyst vide his report dated 28.10.2016 opined the sample as misbranded as the same was without declaration of complete address of manufacturer being in violation of Regulation Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97113668/ 3 2.2.2.6(i) of the FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011. 10. Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (P&L) Regulations reads as under : 2.2.2(6) Labelling of Pre packaged Foods FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 11 (i) Name and complete address of the manufacturer The name and complete address of the manufacturer and the manufacturing unit if these are located at different places and in case the manufacturer is not the packer or bottler, the name and complete address of the packing or bottling unit as the case may be shall be declared on every package of food; 11. It would be pertinent to mention here that Section 23(1) FSS Act requires that no one shall manufacture, distribute, sell any packaged food products which is not labelled as per regulations. Section 23(1) reads as under: "23. Packaging and labelling of foods.(1) No person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale or despatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not marked and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations: Provided that the labels shall not contain any statement, claim, design or device which is false or misleading in any particular concerning the food products contained in the package or concerning the quantity or the nutritive value implying medicinal or therapeutic claims or in relation to the place of origin of the said food products." 12. Further, such noncompliance renders a packaged food article misbranded in terms of Section 3(1)(zf)(c)(i) of FSS Act. FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 8 of 11 13. Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act casts a responsibility on FBO not to sell misbranded food article. Said provision reads as under: 26.Responsibilities of the Food business operator. ..... (2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food - ..... (ii)which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter; or" 14. Section 27(3)(c) FSS Act fastens liability for sale etc. of misbranded food article. Said provision reads as under: "27. Liability of the Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers. ..... (3)The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is ..... Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97113668/ 4 (c)misbranded; or"
